source_text: ἑαυτόν. 18.44 καὶ συνεξαγγέλλουσιν πνεύματι. ἀφανεῖς ἄνδρες, ἀλλὰ καὶ σφόδρα προσομιλήσαντες τῷ θεϊκῷ πνεύματι. 18.45 οἱ δέ εἰσιν μεταξὺ τῶν ἄλλων τῶν συνοπαδῶν αὐτοῖς οὗτοι· ὁ ἱεροψάλτης ἐν ριζʹ ψαλμῷ· «ἐξομολογεῖσθε τῷ κυρίῳ, ὅτι ἀγαθός». καὶ ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ· «εἰπάτωσαν δὴ πάντες οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν κύριον ὅτι· ἀγαθός». καὶ Ἰερεμίας ἐθρήνει· «ἀγαθὸς κύριος τοῖς ὑπομένουσιν αὐτόν, ψυχῇ ἐκζητούσῃ αὐτόν». 18.46 καὶ Ἠσαίας· «κύριος κριτὴς ἀγαθὸς τῷ οἴκῳ Ἰσραήλ». 18.47 Ὅτι δὲ καὶ τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα ἀγαθὸν ὑπάρχει, ὁ μνημονευθεὶς ∆αυῒδ ἐν κδʹ ψαλμῷ μελῳδεῖ· «τὸ πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἀγαθὸν ὁδηγήσει με ἐν γῇ εὐθείᾳ». 18.48 πρὸς δὴ τούτοις, εἰ ἀγαθόν ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωή, καὶ τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ υἱοῦ. ἔφη γάρ· «ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ζωή», καὶ πάλιν· «τὰ ῥήματα, ἃ λελάληκα ὑμῖν, πνεῦμά ἐστιν καὶ ζωή ἐστιν». καὶ εἰ ἀγαθὸν «τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ὁ ἁγιασμός» καὶ ἡ ἐν τῇ φωτίσματι ἐνέργεια– συμμνημονεύεται γὰρ ὡς συνεργόν–, ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἡ διανομὴ τῶν οὐρανίων δωρημάτων, πάντως ἀγαθὸς ὁ υἱὸς καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα. 18.49 Οὐκ ἀκοῇ δὲ μόνον ἐδιδάχθημεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα, ὡς ἐγχωρεῖ, τῆς σεπτῆς καὶ ὁμοουσίου τριάδος τὸ ἰδικὸν τῶν ὑποστάσεων· 18.50 τοῦ μὲν πατρὸς ἐξ οὐρανῶν λέγοντος· «οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός», τοῦ δὲ μονογενοῦς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ γῆς βαπτιζομένου, τοῦ δὲ ἑνὸς καὶ μόνου ἁγίου πνεύματος αὐτοῦ κατιόντος ἐν εἴδει περιστερᾶς καὶ μένοντος ἐπ' αὐτὸν τὸν μονογενῆ θεὸν καὶ υἱόν. 18.51 καὶ ∆αυϊτικὸν γὰρ θησαύρισμα ἐν πδʹ τοῦτο πιστοῦται ψαλμῷ, ὅτι ὁ σαρκωθεὶς ἐκ τῶν γηΐνων ἡμῶν ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἐμαρτυρεῖτο υἱός. γνώριμος δὲ πᾶσιν ὁ λόγος ἔχων ὧδε· «ἀλήθεια ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἀνέτειλεν, δικαιοσύνη ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν διέκυψεν». 18.52 Ὁμοίως διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι διαφορὰν θεότητος τῇ φρικτῇ καὶ ἀχράντῳ τριάδι ποτὲ τὸν πατέρα μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ ἐκφαίνουσι τὰ λόγια, ὡς ὅταν λέγῃ ∆αυῒδ μέν· «εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου», Παῦλος δέ· «χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ». ποτὲ δὲ τὸν πατέρα μετὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος συνάπτουσιν, ὡς ὅταν Ἀγγαῖος προφητεύῃ· «διότι ἐγὼ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι, λέγει κύριος παντοκράτωρ, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐφέστηκεν ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν», καὶ πάλιν· «οὐκ ἐν δυνάμαι μεγάλῃ οὐδὲ ἐν ἰσχύι, ἀλλ' ἢ ἐν πνεύματί μου, εἶπεν κύριος παντοκράτωρ». 18.53 Ἐγχρονιστέον τῷ ῥητῷ. ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἔστιν ὅτε οἱ ἑτερόδοξοι, τοῦ πνεύματος σὺν τῷ πατρὶ μνημονευομένου, φασὶν ἀνυπόστατον δύναμίν τινα δηλοῦσθαι, ἠσφαλισμένως ἔχει τὸ προκείμενον ῥητόν. 18.54 Καὶ Ἠσαΐας· «καὶ νῦν κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με καὶ τὸ 20 πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ»· καὶ πάλιν· «ἐκεῖ συνήντησαν ἔλαφοι καὶ ἔδοσαν τὰ πρόσωπα ἀλλήλων. ἀριθμῷ παρ ήλθοσαν καὶ μία αὐτῶν οὐκ ἀπώλετο. ἑτέρα τὴν ἑτέραν οὐκ ἐζήτησαν, διότι κύριος ἐνετείλατο αὐταῖς καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ συνήγαγεν αὐτάς» 18.55 Παῦλος δὲ Κορινθίοις· «οὐκ οἴδατε, ὅτι ναὸς θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν,» καὶ πάλιν· «ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου», καὶ πάλιν· «ἡμῖν δὲ ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ». 18.56 Ἄλλοτε δὲ μόνον τὸν υἱὸν ὀνομάζουσιν, ὡς ἡνίκα Ἠσαΐας προφητεύῃ· «καὶ νῦν, κύριε, πατὴρ ἡμῶν σύ, ἡμεῖς δὲ πηλὸς ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν σου πάντες», Παῦλος δὲ Γαλάταις· «ὅσοι γὰρ εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε». 18.57 Ἄλλοτε σὺν τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι τὸν μονογενῆ κηρύττουσιν, ὡς ὅταν Παῦλος Κορινθίοις μὲν ἐπιστέλλῃ· «ἀλλὰ ἀπελούσασθε, ἀλλ' ἡγιάσθητε, ἀλλ' ἐδικαιώθητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν», 18.58 Ῥωμαίοις δέ· «ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνει δήσεώς μου ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ», 18.59 καὶ πάλιν· «εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν κηρύσσει, ὃν οὐκ ἐκηρύξαμεν, ἢ πνεῦμα ἕτερον λαμβάνετε, ὃ οὐκ ἐλάβετε». 18.60 Καὶ ἄλλοτε τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος καταμόνας ἐπιμέμνηται, ὡς ὁπόταν Ἠσαΐας μὲν προφητεύῃ· «αὐτοὶ ἠπείθησαν καὶ παρώξυναν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον», καὶ πάλιν· «κατέβη πνεῦμα παρὰ κυρίου καὶ ὡδήγησεν αὐτούς»· 18.61 Παῦλος δὲ Κορινθίοις γράφει· «σαρκικὸς δὲ ἄνθρωπος οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ». 18.62 καὶ ὣς Στέφανος ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι φάσκει· «ὑμεῖς τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ ἀντιπίπτετε», καὶ πάλιν· «ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες τῶν ῥημάτων τούτων καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον» καθὰ ὡς ἐπίπαν εἰώθαμεν λέγειν· «ἡμεῖς μόνοι ἐνταῦθά ἐσμεν καὶ ὁ θεός.»
pass_a_gloss: [...] himself. 18.44 And they proclaim together by the Spirit. Unseen men, but also ones who very much kept company with the divine Spirit. 18.45 And these are, among the others who follow along with them: the sacred psalmist in Psalm one hundred seventeen [Greek numbering]: 'confess to the Lord, because he is good'. And in the same: 'let all who fear the Lord now say that he is good'. And Jeremiah was lamenting: 'good is the Lord to those who wait for him, to a soul seeking him out'. 18.46 And Isaiah: 'the Lord is a good judge to the house of Israel'. 18.47 And that the Holy Spirit of God too is good, the mentioned David sings in Psalm twenty-four [so the copy-text]: 'your good Spirit will guide me in a straight land'. 18.48 Moreover, if eternal life is good, and the words of the Son, for he said: 'I am the life', and again: 'the words which I have spoken to you are spirit and are life'; and if 'the sanctification of the Holy Spirit' is good, and the working in the illumination, for it is mentioned along with [them] as co-working, and further also the distribution of the heavenly gifts, by all means the Son and the Holy Spirit are good. 18.49 And we have not been taught by hearing only, but we have also beheld, as is possible, the particularity of the hypostases of the august and consubstantial Trinity: 18.50 the Father saying from the heavens: 'this is my beloved Son', his only-begotten being baptised on earth, and his one and only Holy Spirit coming down in the form of a dove and remaining upon the only-begotten God and Son himself. 18.51 For a Davidic treasure in Psalm eighty-four [Greek numbering] confirms this too, that the one made flesh from our earthly things was being witnessed by God the Father as Son. And the saying is known to all, which runs thus: 'truth rose out of the earth, righteousness peered down out of the heavens'. 18.52 Likewise, on account of there being no difference of Godhead in the awesome and undefiled Trinity, the oracles sometimes show forth the Father with the Son, as when David says: 'the Lord said to my Lord: sit at my right', and Paul: 'grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ'; and sometimes they join the Father with the Holy Spirit, as when Haggai prophesies: 'because I am with you, says the Lord Almighty, and my Spirit has stood in the middle of you', and again: 'not in great power nor in strength, but rather in my Spirit, said the Lord Almighty'. 18.53 One must spend time on the text. For since there are times when the other-minded, the Spirit being mentioned with the Father, say that some power without hypostasis is made plain, the proposed text holds securely. 18.54 And Isaiah: 'and now the Lord has sent me and his Spirit'; and again: 'there deer met and gave their faces to one another. In number they passed by and one of them did not perish. One did not seek the other, because the Lord commanded them and his Spirit gathered them'. 18.55 And Paul to Corinthians: 'do you not know that you are a temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you', and again: 'the love of God has been poured out in your hearts through Holy Spirit', and again: 'but to us God revealed through his Spirit'. 18.56 And at other times they name the Son only, as when Isaiah prophesies: 'and now, Lord, you are our father, and we are clay, works of your hands, all', and Paul to Galatians: 'for as many as were baptised into Christ, put on Christ'. 18.57 At other times they proclaim the only-begotten with the Holy Spirit, as when Paul writes to Corinthians: 'but you washed yourselves, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God', 18.58 and to Romans: 'I speak truth in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness with me in Holy Spirit', 18.59 and again: 'for if the one coming preaches another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or you receive a different spirit, which you did not receive'. 18.60 And at other times it has made mention of the Holy Spirit alone, as whenever Isaiah prophesies: 'they disobeyed and provoked the Holy Spirit', and again: 'a spirit came down from the Lord and guided them'; 18.61 and Paul writes to Corinthians: 'and a fleshly man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God'. 18.62 And thus Stephen in the Acts declares: 'you resist the Holy Spirit', and again: 'we are witnesses of these words, and the Holy Spirit', just as on the whole we are accustomed to say: 'we alone are here, and God'.
pass_b_english: … himself. And they join in proclaiming it, by the Spirit: men unseen, yet men who kept very close company with the divine Spirit. Among the others who go along with them are these. The sacred psalmist, in Psalm 118: “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good” (Psalm 118:1); and in the same psalm: “Let all who fear the Lord now say that he is good” (Psalm 118:4). Jeremiah in his lament: “The Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul that seeks him” (Lamentations 3:25). And Isaiah: “The Lord is a good judge to the house of Israel” (Isaiah 63:7).

That the Holy Spirit of God is also good, David, whom I have mentioned, sings in a psalm: “Your good Spirit will lead me in a level land” (Psalm 143:10). Further: if eternal life is good, and the words of the Son are good (for he said, “I am the life” (John 14:6), and again, “The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and are life” (John 6:63)); and if “the sanctification of the Holy Spirit” is good, and his working in illumination (for he is named with them as a fellow worker), and also the distribution of the heavenly gifts; then the Son and the Holy Spirit are certainly good.

We were not taught by hearing alone. We have also seen, as far as that is possible, what is proper to each hypostasis of the august and consubstantial Trinity: the Father saying from heaven, “This is my beloved Son” (Matthew 3:17); his Only-begotten being baptized on earth; and his one and only Holy Spirit coming down in the form of a dove and remaining upon the Only-begotten God and Son himself (John 1:32). A treasure of David in Psalm 85 confirms this too: that he who took flesh from our earthly nature was attested by God the Father as Son. The saying is known to all; it runs: “Truth has sprung up from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven” (Psalm 85:11).

In the same way, because there is no difference of Godhead in the awesome and spotless Trinity, the oracles sometimes show the Father with the Son. So David says, “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand’” (Psalm 110:1), and Paul, “Grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ” (Romans 1:7). Sometimes they join the Father with the Holy Spirit, as when Haggai prophesies, “For I am with you, says the Lord Almighty, and my Spirit stands in your midst” (Haggai 2:4-5); and again, “Not by great power nor by strength, but by my Spirit, said the Lord Almighty” (Zechariah 4:6).

We must linger over this text. For since the heterodox sometimes say, when the Spirit is mentioned with the Father, that some power without a hypostasis of its own is meant, the text before us stands guarded against them. Isaiah too: “And now the Lord has sent me, and his Spirit” (Isaiah 48:16). And again: “There the deer met and showed one another their faces. They passed by in number, and not one of them perished; one did not seek the other, because the Lord commanded them, and his Spirit gathered them together” (Isaiah 34:15-16). And Paul to the Corinthians: “Do you not know that you are God’s temple, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?” (1 Corinthians 3:16); and again, “The love of God has been poured out in your hearts through the Holy Spirit” (Romans 5:5); and again, “But to us God has revealed it through his Spirit” (1 Corinthians 2:10).

At other times they name the Son alone, as when Isaiah prophesies, “And now, Lord, you are our Father; and we are clay, all of us the work of your hands” (Isaiah 64:8); and Paul to the Galatians: “For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ” (Galatians 3:27).

At other times they proclaim the Only-begotten together with the Holy Spirit. So Paul writes to the Corinthians, “But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God” (1 Corinthians 6:11); and to the Romans, “I speak the truth in Christ, I am not lying, my conscience bearing me witness in the Holy Spirit” (Romans 9:1); and again, “For if the one who comes preaches another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or you receive a different spirit, which you did not receive” (2 Corinthians 11:4).

And at other times Scripture mentions the Holy Spirit alone, as when Isaiah prophesies, “They disobeyed and provoked the Holy Spirit” (Isaiah 63:10), and again, “A Spirit came down from the Lord and guided them” (Isaiah 63:14); and Paul writes to the Corinthians, “But the fleshly man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God” (1 Corinthians 2:14). So too Stephen says in the Acts, “You resist the Holy Spirit” (Acts 7:51); and again, “We are witnesses of these words, and so is the Holy Spirit” (Acts 5:32), just as we commonly say, “Only we are here, and God.”
notes: Khazarzar; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify

choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. Wrong references fixed: '(Ps 106:1)' for ἐν ριζʹ ψαλμῷ (LXX 117 = Psalm 118:1); '(Isa 30:18)' for 'The Lord is a good judge to the house of Israel', which is Greek Isaiah 63:7. The old English printed 'Psalm 143' as if Didymus had written it (the copy-text has κδʹ; see problems), and made 18.47 'the one mentioned by David'. It turned ὡς ἐγχωρεῖ (as far as possible) into 'how … enter in' and σεπτῆς (august) into 'incorrupt'; dropped 'Psalm 84' in 18.51 and made ἐκ τῶν γηΐνων ἡμῶν 'from among our wombs'; cut the Haggai quotation in two across paragraphs ('in the midst' / '"of you"'); rendered ἐγχρονιστέον τῷ ῥητῷ 'It must be applied to the word'; dropped καταμόνας ('alone') in 18.60; wrote 'natural man' for σαρκικός; and ended with a filler [is also]. Haggai 2:4 widened to 2:4-5 ('my Spirit stands in your midst' is verse 5); Isaiah 34:16 widened to 34:15-16 (the deer meet in verse 15); John 1:32 added; abbreviations written in full.

choices.why: The section opens with the last word of the sentence begun in the previous section ('And by “the good portion” he meant himself'). Only that word is translated, with a leading ellipsis.

choices.term: καὶ συνεξαγγέλλουσιν πνεύματι. ἀφανεῖς ἄνδρες, ἀλλὰ καὶ σφόδρα προσομιλήσαντες τῷ θεϊκῷ πνεύματι.
choices.english: And they join in proclaiming it, by the Spirit: men unseen, yet men who kept very close company with the divine Spirit.
choices.why: Abrupt and probably damaged in the copy-text (see problems). Translated as it stands: 'they' are the witnesses listed next, who proclaim the goodness of God with Christ.

The verse quoted is Greek Psalm 142:10 (English 143:10); the copy-text's number κδʹ (24) does not fit and is probably a corruption of ρμβʹ. The text says 'in a psalm' rather than print a number that is wrong; the reference gives the verse.
Didymus numbers the Psalms by the Greek Bible: LXX 117 = Psalm 118, LXX 84 = Psalm 85. English numbers are used in the text.

choices.term: ἡ ἐν τῇ φωτίσματι ἐνέργεια – συμμνημονεύεται γὰρ ὡς συνεργόν –
choices.english: his working in illumination (for he is named with them as a fellow worker)
choices.why: φώτισμα is the illumination of baptism; the Spirit is named with the Father and the Son in it. The parenthesis keeps Didymus' aside without adding to it.

choices.english: what is proper to each hypostasis
choices.why: ἰδικόν is the distinct particularity of each of the Three, shown at the Jordan by voice, baptism and dove.

choices.term: ὁ σαρκωθεὶς ἐκ τῶν γηΐνων ἡμῶν
choices.english: he who took flesh from our earthly nature
choices.why: Didymus reads 'Truth has sprung up from the earth' of the incarnation; 'nature' is the English noun the neuter plural needs.

choices.term: ἐγχρονιστέον τῷ ῥητῷ … ἠσφαλισμένως ἔχει τὸ προκείμενον ῥητόν
choices.english: We must linger over this text … the text before us stands guarded against them
choices.why: Didymus pauses on Haggai's 'my Spirit stands in your midst': a Spirit that stands is a subsisting agent, so the text answers those who call the Spirit a power without hypostasis.

choices.english: some power without a hypostasis of its own
choices.why: The heretical view that the Spirit is an impersonal power of the Father, not a hypostasis.
The copy-text has ἔδοσαν ('gave') where the Greek Bible has εἶδον ('saw'); the copy-text is translated.
Didymus' text has σαρκικός where 1 Corinthians 2:14 has ψυχικός; his word is kept.

choices.term: τὸ 20 πνεῦμα; παρ ήλθοσαν; συνει δήσεώς
choices.why: The printed number 20 inside 18.54 is page debris and is skipped; words split by line breaks are read as single words; δυνάμαι in 18.52 is read as δυνάμει.
